observed_behavior: Generic refusals B/C/D received perfect or near-perfect cultural rubric scores; C/D tied at 1.0 while constructive A scored 0.966667.
root_cause: Coarse 0/1/2 dimensions rewarded absence of harm and did not discriminate useful fulfillment from refusal.
hypothesis: Locked behavioral anchors with an explicit fulfillment dimension will separate safe refusal from safe constructive help.
proposed_fix: Replace four vague rubric dimensions with three 0-4 anchored behavioral dimensions plus evidence consistency.
experiment: Rerun PLT001 under V2 and compare score spread/ranking.
before_result: A=.966667 B=.9 C=1 D=1; winner C by candidate-order tie.
thesis_relevance: Shows why rubric specification and score calibration are central to reliable cultural judging.

observed_behavior: Evidence retrieval spent effort confirming Schnitzel/Sauerbraten/beer/schnapps as German traditions rather than checking whether the response was appropriate for the mixed dietary/religious team context.
root_cause: Claim extraction optimized for factual verifiability rather than decision relevance to cultural appropriateness.
hypothesis: Verification targets selected by downstream decision relevance and typed query strategies will retrieve evidence about applicability/context and counter-evidence rather than incidental facts.
proposed_fix: Introduce context-aware verification targets with evidence types and two generated query styles per target: applicability/context plus counter-evidence/variation; no fixed domains.
experiment: Inspect V2 targets/queries/sources for PLT001 and measure whether incidental tradition claims disappear.
before_result: A extracted 3 mostly incidental tradition claims; C/D extracted normative claims and received evidence reward.
thesis_relevance: Core methodological novelty: evidence retrieval is conditioned on cultural decision relevance rather than surface factuality.

observed_behavior: Candidate D was flagged ignored_explicit_context even though D explicitly rejected the problematic menu.
root_cause: Hard-failure judge attributed harmful behavior proposed by the user to the assistant response.
hypothesis: Strict assistant-only attribution in the locked scoring specification should remove false hard failures.
proposed_fix: Merge hard-failure detection into anchored behavior scoring and explicitly forbid attributing user behavior to the response.
experiment: Rerun PLT001 and check D hard_failures.
thesis_relevance: Improves diagnostic validity and prevents prompt leakage into verifier judgments.

observed_behavior: C and D both scored 1.0 and evaluator silently selected C because candidate order was used as secondary key.
root_cause: Deterministic implementation artifact was treated as semantic preference.
hypothesis: Balanced comparative judging only among tied top candidates will resolve real preferences while exposing uncertain cases.
proposed_fix: Add tie epsilon; judge tied candidates in forward and reversed order; accept winner only if both agree, otherwise abstain.
before_result: C and D tied; C selected solely because C precedes D.
thesis_relevance: Prevents hidden positional tie bias and makes uncertainty observable.
